items.item: 5b. Outro: map turns to 04 on 读, next-episode line on 看
items.change: Not fixable in my files. Throughout the outro (346.4–351.9) the map stays focused on 03 and the next-episode line never appears. Cause, checked on the live stage (probe of scene-gtd-outro): film/series.js:204 computes `next = MAP[i + 1] && UNITS[MAP[i + 1].id]`, but UNITS is built from Film.units, and on a standalone stage that holds only the episode's own unit (here ['gtd']). So `next` is undefined: the 读 focus toggle is never registered, and the .sr-next box gets empty text and shows at the segment start (opacity 1 at 347.5 with innerHTML ''). The end card avoids this with `UNITS[b.next] || b.nextInfo`, and the ep03 end block carries nextInfo {no:'04', title:'把错误摆上桌面'}. Suggested shared fix at series.js:204: fall back to the end block's nextInfo, keeping the MAP id for the focus toggle, e.g. `const nm = MAP[i + 1], next = nm && (UNITS[nm.id] || (endCard && endCard.nextInfo && Object.assign({ id: nm.id }, endCard.nextInfo)));`. Every standalone episode with a following one probably has the same problem.
items.evidence: outro-turn-next.png (346.4, 346.6, 346.8, 347.2, 349.4, 349.7, 350.0, 350.6, 351.4): 03 stays blue, nothing below the map. Probe output: at 347.5 and 350.5 the cols are ['iu','im','gtd*','pr','lt'] and .sr-next is '' at opacity 1; Series.units keys = ['gtd'].

items.item: 8. Verify new outro and hold
items.change: No change in my files. The join and the end handover work, but two outro beats are missing because of a defect in film/series.js outro(). In a standalone assembly, Film.units, and so UNITS, holds only the episode's own unit (on the ep01 stage Object.keys(Series.units) is ['iu']). So next = MAP[i + 1] && UNITS[MAP[i + 1].id] is undefined. As a result: (a) the focus never turns to 02 on 读 and stays on 01 through 409.9; (b) the next-episode line is an empty box (on the stage .sr-next innerHTML is '', because o.last is undefined) shown at segment start, so nothing appears on 看 (406.81). The end card does not have this problem because it falls back to b.nextInfo. Suggested fix in series.js:204: const nid = MAP[i + 1] && MAP[i + 1].id, next = nid && (UNITS[nid] || (endCard && endCard.nextInfo)); then compare c.dataset.unit with nid instead of next.id in the onFrame toggle. This probably affects every standalone episode except the last.
